messages.subject: Path analysis in Three piecewise Growth Trajectory Model
parts:
Hello all, I have a few doubts in regard to analyzing growth trajectory of my outcome variable. I am posting my doubts separately in seperate posts.

This posts concerns my doubt about the following research question:

Explain the factors affecting the outcome variable, i.e. Path analysis [according to the theoretical path model in the attaached diagram] ; 
and, analyze whether factors affect the outcome variable differently in different months.
Note: We concluded on using three-piece latent growth trajectory model as we have both theoretical as well as empirical justification for doing so.

Nature of dataset: Panel dataset [601 observations x 11 months]

Continuous Variables
  • Outcome Variable: outcomeVar
  • age
Dichotomous variables
  • literacy [1/0] 
  • landown [1/0] 
  • prodAsset [1/0]
  • nimB [1/0]
  • durable [1/0]
  • Occupation variables :  OccupA [1/0], OccupB [1/0]  [reference category: OccupC(1/0) such that OccupA and OccupB==0]
All the variables are time-varying.

Number suffix in the variables refer to month 2 - month 12 [we have discarded the observations from month 1 from the analysis due to survey issues]


My Question
  • Do you think the codes are correctly written, in terms of any other options that I might need to add?
    • Since the Occupation variable is a mediator variable, and is dichotomous, I have included the option "ordered = " in the fit command. I had earlier estimated it without this option. Please guide me if I am correct to have included the option. 
    • Also, do you think I should rather fix the threshold for occupation variable?
  • The fit indices of this model is poor, perhaps, due to a large number of parameters to be estimates [majority of which - especially, the indirect effects, are insignificant]. 
    • I just wanted to confirm if it would make sense to gradually remove those direct and indirect effects for specific months for which parameters are insignificant to improve the model fit indices? 
      • If not, what could be the alternative strategy to improve the model fit indices?


Here are my codes.
